newsitem.title: USA: Dresdner urges U.S. bank law changes.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner urges U.S. bank law changes.

text.p: Germany's second largest commercial bank, Dresdner Bank AG, called for changes in U.S. legislation to open the way for universal banking.

In a speech delivered in Washington Sunday, Dresdner Bank chief executive Juergen Sarrazin said he had been optimistic when he attended the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank one year ago that U.S. legislation was gradually moving toward universal banking.
"Unfortunately, it seems that in the meantime this legislative reform has come to a halt, despite serious efforts on all sides," he said.

Sarrazin said Dresdner, as many other banks, suffered from this as it made its activities less efficient, adding: "Like many U.S. banks, we, as a non-U.S. bank, are acutely aware of the costs and inefficiencies for our U.S. operations because of the current legislative and regulatory framework."

"Like U.S. banks therefore, we take encouragement from recent proposals of U.S. regulators to further relax some provisions separating commercial and investment banking," he added. "We support them strongly but, even more strongly, would like to see definitive legislative solutions," he added.
